matchstick.title: Transform V into X by repositioning one stick
matchstick.principle: If a V (two diagonal sticks) appears, moving one of its diagonal sticks to intersect the other creates an X, changing the numeral from 5 to 10. This increases the value of the numeral by 5 with a single stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V is present and increasing its value could help balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Tried to change V into L by moving a stick, which fails because a single stick cannot turn V into L.

matchstick.title: Move a vertical I‑stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: A vertical I‑stick can be detached from a numeral containing I's and attached to another numeral, effectively moving a value‑1 stick between numbers.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by one and moving a single I between numerals could correct the balance.
matchstick.example: Attempted to move a diagonal stick from V to I, which does not produce a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore relocating a stick within the same character, as this often yields a valid transformation without altering other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, try moves that keep the stick inside its original character.
matchstick.example: Ignored the possibility of moving a stick from + to a numeral, focusing only on intra‑character moves.

matchstick.title: Validate source and target symbols after a stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the symbol you removed it from and the symbol you added it to must remain valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing any stick relocation, check the resulting symbols for validity.
matchstick.example: Created a single diagonal stick as a new symbol, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid creating single angled sticks (invalid numerals)
matchstick.principle: A lone diagonal stick does not correspond to any Roman numeral; V and X require two diagonal sticks each.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever moving diagonal sticks, verify that V and X retain both required diagonals.
matchstick.example: Removed one diagonal from V, leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert + to - by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present, removing its vertical stick turns it into a minus sign; the removed stick can be added to a numeral to increase its value, often balancing an equation where the RHS is too large.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is unbalanced and a plus sign appears, consider converting + to - and using the vertical stick to adjust a numeral.
matchstick.example: Only tried moving sticks within numerals, missing the move that changes + to - and adds the stick to II.

matchstick.title: Create a new numeral by moving a stick to a new position (reordering)
matchstick.principle: A stick can be detached from an existing numeral and placed at a new location, forming a new numeral before another, thereby changing the order and numeric value (e.g., moving an I stick left of V to turn VI into IV).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral can be split or a stick can be repositioned to form a new character that changes the numeric value, especially to reduce an oversized side.
matchstick.example: Assumed sticks cannot be moved to create a new character, missing the solution of turning VI into IV.

matchstick.title: Consider inter‑character stick relocation when intra‑character moves fail
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character stick move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character (including operators) to another character, as this can change both the operator and numeral values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character relocation attempts without success.
matchstick.example: Focused only on intra‑character moves and concluded no solution, overlooking the needed move from + to II.
